description: How the first-contact harvest classes Wikidata statements (25-LIVES-AND-PLAYGROUND.md section 10). Defaults go by datatype: external-id is an identifier; wikibase-item is a relationship (mapped to a predicate through the predicate registry's wikidata mappings, otherwise unmapped and kept); time is a dated claim; other literals are attributes. The lists below override the defaults. Every PID here was checked against Wikidata's own label when the harvest report resolves it.

notes.P1343: described by source stays a relationship (registry: describedBy), Wikidata's own bibliography of the entity: input for the Subject 'Read more' list (25 section 8)
notes.P1038: relative stays an unmapped relationship until its kinship qualifier (P1039) is mapped; legacy code lost that qualifier
notes.kinds: Wikidata 'instance of' classes mapped to kinds, each class checked against its Wikidata label on 2026-10-13 from the classes of Mark Antony's one-hop targets; a target whose classes are not listed goes to the agent's judgement, never guessed. A historical country, an empire, or a form of government is left to the agent (a polity is neither simply a Place nor a Group). Extended 2026-10-13 from the classes of the expansion's agent queue, each checked against its label. Deliberately left to the agent: US city classes (a Wikidata statement points to Alexandria, Virginia), temporal entity, former administrative territorial entity; polities (historical country, ancient civilization) wait for the Polity kind (registry v9).
notes.federations: External identifiers kept as AuthorityRecords (curator, 2026-10-13: only federations we use); the rest stay readable in the preserved record. Checked labels: P1415 is the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, not the Oxford Classical Dictionary as legacy code assumed.
notes.noiseClasses: Wikimedia disambiguation page: a statement pointing at one is a Wikidata error, dropped by rule.
